subject: Proposed SLA amendments: maintenance blackout window & credit cap
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-06T16:15:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA language / maintenance window

Aditya —

Thanks for sending over the draft MSA + Order Form. Our legal and ops teams reviewed and attached a set of redlines (Acme_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf). High level calls out:

- Uptime target: we are asking for 99.95% monthly availability for API endpoints covering customer-facing production traffic.
- Service credits: credits calculated pro-rata by minute of total outage and applied to the affected product line; monthly cap requested at 50% of the monthly fees.
- Response & mitigation: 1 hour initial response for Sev1 incidents, 4 hours to mitigate or provide workaround; Sev2 acknowledged within 4 hours.
- Maintenance windows: limit scheduled maintenance to a single 4-hour window per month, with 72 hours advance notice; blackout periods during launch week or migrations where no scheduled maintenance permitted.
- Auditables: we require access to uptime reports and raw incident logs for the preceding 12 months as part of acceptance.

We redlined the order form and included language changes. Our legal contact is cc'd — Rachel can walk through the specifics if helpful.

Can your side confirm whether Redwood can accept proportional credits (vs whole-account credits) and the proposed uptime number? If not, please propose a concrete counter.

Best,
Sam

Attachments: Acme_SLA_redlines_v3.pdf

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmecorp.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-06T20:02:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA language / maintenance window

Sam — thanks for the detailed pass and the PDF. We appreciate the clarity.

Quick read and proposed trade-offs from our side:

- Uptime: we can commit to 99.9% per month for the endpoints in scope. We are open to discussing a 99.95% target for specific critical routes if Acme agrees to a targeted scope and larger commit (reserved capacity) — otherwise the operational variability makes 99.95% difficult to guarantee across burst traffic patterns.
- Credits: we can accept proportional credits but need to limit the monthly cap to 30% of fees. We also prefer a tiered credit table (e.g., 5% / 10% / 20%) rather than one linear minute-by-minute calculation to keep invoicing predictable.
- Response SLAs: we will commit to a 30-minute acknowledgement for Sev1, with an operational mitigation target of 2 hours for incidents caused by our infrastructure. For Sev1s caused by customer-side misconfiguration we will provide support but not credits.
- Maintenance: we can support one 6-hour scheduled maintenance window per month (UTC-based) with 72 hours notice. We can agree to blackout windows for documented launches and migrations with <n> exceptions for emergency security patches.
- Audit logs & compliance: we will provide SOC2 Type II reports and an availability dashboard with 30-day retention by default; we can discuss extended retention as a paid add-on.

Next steps: Marcus / Dev — please review the attached redlines and call out technical limitations (esp. on per-route 99.95%). Rachel / Sam — happy to jump on a 30-minute alignment call. Suggested times: Tue Apr 9 10:00 or Wed Apr 10 15:00 PT.

Thanks,
Aditya
Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmecorp.com>
To: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-07T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA language / maintenance window (Acme redlines)

Aditya / team —

Thanks for the quick response. I reviewed your counter-proposals with our legal ops team and attached a tracked-redlines Word doc (acme_redlines_tracked.docx) that includes the following asks and clarifications:

- Service credits: instead of a flat tier, we proposed language that credits only the "affected capacity" (i.e., if a single route is degraded, credit applies only to that product line). This is to avoid situations where a narrow outage triggers a full-account credit.
- Cap: we are willing to move from 50% to 40% if Redwood reduces the definition of "affected capacity" to specific product routes and provides a monthly usage report.
- Root cause & RCA: we will accept credits only after a shared RCA that confirms the outage was within Redwood's control.
- Auditables / evidence: we need access to hourly uptime time-series for the last 12 months and incident logs (redacted as necessary). We also asked for an explicit commitment around SOC2 Type II annual delivery and an SLA for forensic log exports (5 business days).
- Maintenance blackout: we absolutely need a clause that prohibits scheduled maintenance during a customer-declared 7-day launch window; emergency patches can be excluded with written notice within 24 hours of scheduling.

We can accept a tiered credit structure in principle; the attached doc suggests 10%/25%/50% tiers tied to outage thresholds, and a 40% cap. Please review our tracked changes and let us know which points are non-starters for Redwood.

If it helps, we can have our ops director join the call.

Rachel
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp

Attachments: acme_redlines_tracked.docx

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-07T11:12:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Re: SLA language / maintenance window (Acme redlines)

Lauren — forwarding Acme's redlines and Rachel's note. Key items I want legal to review and propose final language on:

1) Credit scope: Acme wants credits limited to "affected capacity" but a 40% cap; they will accept lower caps if we narrow scope. We prefer a cap no higher than 30% and a tiered table.
2) Uptime target: they asked for 99.95% across production; we suggested 99.9% unless they buy reserved capacity. Is 99.95% acceptable if scoped to specific routes?
3) Maintenance blackout: they require a 7-day launch blackout; they also want emergency patches excluded but with 24-hour notice for scheduling — how do we quantify "emergency"?
4) Evidence & SOC2: they want access to logs and SOC2 Type II annually and forensic exports within 5 business days. Confirm what we can commit to operationally and whether we need a carve-out on data export charges.

Attached are the redline PDF and Rachel's tracked Word doc. Please draft a response we can send back (I can join the call).

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>

Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acmecorp.com>, Rachel Gomez <rachel.gomez@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2027-04-08T07:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Re: SLA language / maintenance window (Acme redlines)

Aditya / team —

Thanks for the forward. I reviewed Acme's tracked redlines and Rachel's summary. Below is the recommended negotiation stance and proposed language points:

- Uptime target: counter to 99.9% monthly availability for the full account, with an option for 99.95% for explicitly listed "critical routes" if Acme signs up for dedicated/reserved capacity in the Order Form. Draft language: "Provider agrees to 99.9% monthly availability for Services; for routes listed in Schedule A (Critical Routes) availability commitment shall be 99.95% if Customer accepts Reserved Capacity terms."

- Service credits: accept proportional, tiered credits tied to demonstrated outage to affected product lines only. Propose tiered table (sample):
  * 0 - 30 minutes downtime: 5% credit
  * 30 - 180 minutes: 15% credit
  * >180 minutes: 30% credit
  Cap the total monthly credit at 30% of the monthly recurring fees. Draft language should require RCA confirming Provider responsibility before credits apply.

- Response & mitigation: commit to 30 minute acknowledgement for Sev1; commit to a 4-hour mitigation target to match engineering practices and to be conservative. Keep credit applicability tied to Provider-controlled failures.

- Maintenance & blackout: accept a 7-day launch blackout so long as Customer provides written notice 10 business days in advance and includes a definition for "emergency maintenance" limited to security-critical patches or immediate remediation actions required to prevent data loss. Emergency maintenance must be communicated within 24 hours and will be limited in scope.

- Evidence & SOC2: commit to providing SOC2 Type II annually and to share availability dashboards and aggregated uptime data for rolling 12 months. Forensic log exports can be produced within 10 business days; additional export/processing time and costs may be billed.

Next steps: I will produce tracked language for Sections 5 (Availability), 6 (Credits), and 9 (Maintenance) and send to Sam/Rachel for review. Please let me know if you want alternate credit tiers or a higher/lower cap — my current recommended cap is 30% as it balances customer protection and commercial viability.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
